issues.description: Fields: the problem statement (descriptive text) names two lecture attributes as 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents', while the UML in the problem statement and the reference solution declare the attributes as 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents'. Template file contains a TODO to add attributes but does not define names. This mismatch means students reading the descriptive text may implement fields with the shorter names and wrong constructor parameter order, while tests and the UML expect the 'numberOf...' identifiers and a constructor following that order. The inconsistency can cause compilation failures in tests or failing automated checks because identifier names and constructor parameter ordering differ between description and solution/UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute identifiers consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: update the descriptive text in problem_statement.md (lines listing attribute names and any example sentences) to use 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' and explicitly state the constructor parameter order matching the UML: (String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors). Ensure any example toString() or task descriptions also use these exact identifiers. Alternatively (less preferred) rename the UML and solution fields to 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' and update constructor/tests accordingly. Keep the chosen naming consistent in template, UML, problem text, and solution.

issues.description: Concept: the attributes that hold the counts of enrolled and guest students. The problem statement text (line 17) lists the attributes as 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents', whereas the UML diagram and the solution implementation declare these attributes as 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents'. The template's Lecture.java only contains a TODO referencing the UML but does not spell out names. This inconsistent naming of the same conceptual attributes can confuse students about which exact field names (and therefore which getter/setter names) the tests and UML expect, causing unnecessary trial-and-error or failing tests if students implement the shorter names.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute names consistent across artifacts. Update problem_statement.md to list 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' (replacing 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents') to match the UML and solution, and clarify the template TODO comment to explicitly mention the expected field names. Alternatively, if shorter names were intended, update the UML, tests, and solution to the shorter names — but prefer aligning the problem text to the existing UML/tests/solution.
